Since there are $R$ components (rank) and each vector $v_r^3$ has dimension $K$, the resulting matrix $V^3$ has dimensions $K x R$. The evidence supports the definition of the vectors $v_r^3$ and the rank $R$, which directly implies the structure of the factor matrix described in the claim.

In the context of volume rendering, it is used to factorize the 3D (or 4D) radiance field tensor into compact vectors, significantly reducing the memory footprint compared to dense voxel grids [S1][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that in volume rendering, tensor decomposition is used to factorize 3D/4D radiance fields into compact vectors, reducing memory footprint compared to dense voxel grids. Source [S1] explicitly mentions: 'Our tensorial radiance fields can be effectively reconstructed... our tensor factorization reduces space complexity from O(n^3) to O(n) (with CP)... significantly lowering memory footprint.' It also states: 'A tensorial radiance field representation that factorizes density and appearance feature grids into compact vectors using Canonical Polyadic (CP) decomposition.' Source [S3] corroborates this: 'we model the radiance field of a scene as a 4D tensor... factorize the 4D scene tensor into multiple compact low-rank tensor components... leads to a significantly lower memory footprint in comparison to previous and concurrent works that directly optimize per-voxel features.' Both sources confirm the factorization into vectors (specifically CP decomposition) and the reduction in memory footprint compared to dense grids.
